$comment: Which researched candidate is shown at each age: a number picks from content/facts/part-*.json (0 = a, 1 = b); {"redo": i} picks from the second round (content/facts/redo-out-*.json, facts about the age itself). Optional "text" adjusts wording and "kind" re-labels it, without changing the source.

1.text: In a New York lab study, toddlers aged 12 to 19 months averaged 2,368 steps and 17 falls in every hour of free play.

2.text: By 30 months, most toddlers say about 50 words and put two or more together with an action word, like “doggie run”.

3.text: Most three-year-olds can keep a conversation going for two back-and-forth turns, and have started asking “who”, “what”, “where” or “why” questions.

8.text: In a US study, children of five to seven recalled 60% or more of events discussed at age three, while eight- and nine-year-olds recalled under 40%.

11.text: NHS Wales gives 11 as the average age for girls to start puberty.

16.text: In 2007 Austria became the first EU country to lower the voting age to 16 in national elections, from 18.

17.text: Asked about personally meaningful songs, 1,891 people from many countries most often named ones released when they were about 17.

19.text: The mind's raw speed at processing information peaks around 18 or 19; other abilities keep ripening for decades.

23.text: In 1990 the median age at first marriage for US women was 23.9, Census Bureau estimates show.

24.text: In a study of 3,305 StarCraft 2 players aged 16 to 44, age-related slowing of in-game response times began at 24.

33.text: Vocabulary keeps growing through adulthood: between 20 and 60, an average native speaker of American English learns about one new word every two days.

39.text: The Fields Medal, which recognises outstanding mathematical achievement, is kept for the young: a candidate's 40th birthday must not fall before 1 January of the award year.

49.text: A 2015 study put the median age at which American women become grandmothers at 49. In parts of Western Europe it came up to eight years later.

52.text: In the United States, men born in 1926–43 became grandfathers at a median age of 52, according to a 2015 study comparing 25 countries.

54.text: In a worldwide survey of 4,192 people, published in 2012, 74% of those aged 45 to 65 had some grey hair; when it arrives varies with ethnic and geographic origin.

59.text: In January 2026, US workers aged 55 to 64 had been with their current employer for a median of 9.6 years, more than three times as long as those aged 25 to 34.

69.text: In a German-Swiss trial of adults aged 62 to 78, six months of piano lessons improved hearing of speech in noise in the left ear, a gain not seen in a music-listening group.

70.text: In 2025 Denmark voted to raise its state pension age to 70, the highest in Europe, for people born after 1970.

72.text: In a UK survey of over 300,000 adults in 2012 to 2015, people aged 65 to 74 reported the highest average happiness of any age group.

76.text: In the US in 2024, people aged 75 and over spent an average of 46 minutes a day reading for pleasure. Those aged 15 to 19 read for 9 minutes.

79.text: In the US in 2024, adults aged 75 and over spent 7.6 hours a day on leisure and sports, more than any other age group.

80.text: Catholic cardinals who turn 80 before the day the papacy falls vacant do not vote in the conclave that elects the next pope.

84.text: Some local government offices and financial institutions in Japan use earphones that vibrate the ear's cartilage, so staff helping older people need not speak loudly.

85.text: In 2018, the UK's Office for National Statistics projected that the number of people aged 85 and over would double, from 1.6 million in 2016 to 3.2 million by 2041.

86.text: In the UK in 2016 to 2017, 8% of people aged 85 and over were providing informal care to others.

89.text: In US health records de-identified under HIPAA’s ‘safe harbor’ method, 89 is the oldest age that may be shown; older ages are removed or grouped as ‘90 or older’.

94.text: Japan had an estimated 273,000 people aged 94 on 1 October 2024, about three in four of them women.

96.text: In a 1990 study, nine frail nursing-home residents aged up to 96 did eight weeks of weight training, and their strength rose by 174% on average.

98.text: In a study of 29 people aged 90 to 101 in rural southern Italy, the elders reported better mental well-being than their younger relatives.

100.text: Japan counted 153 people aged 100 or over in 1963. In 2026 it counted 107,677.

106.text: British nationals can receive a birthday message from the King at 100 and 105, and then every year after their 105th birthday.

115.text: Sequencing the blood of a 115-year-old woman suggested that most of her white blood cells descended from just two related blood stem cells.
